title: Leading-context fragment pooling and guided eviction for reduced KV footprint
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Observed high GPU memory fragmentation and duplicated KV contents when many requests include similar leading context (system prompts, product descriptions, or canned instructions). This leads to wasted memory, lowered cache hit amplification, and higher per-token cost under sustained concurrency.

Goal: Implement a runtime-level fragment pooling system that identifies identical or highly-similar leading-context segments across requests ("context shards"), normalizes and fingerprints them, stores them as shared, relocatable KV fragments aligned to GPU allocation boundaries, and applies a guided eviction/coalescing strategy to minimize GPU resident memory while preserving high cache hit rates and low tail latency.

Success criteria: net reduction in GPU-resident KV size (measured per node), improved end-to-end token cost for representative workloads, and <=5% p95 latency regression for cold-start requests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New fragment index stores deduplicated context shards with canonical fingerprints; 2) Runtime can attach shared fragments to incoming requests without copying token-by-token into request-local KV; 3) Observed >=20% reduction in KV bytes-resident for web-chat workload (internal benchmark) on production-like concurrency; 4) No regression >5% p95 latency for steady-state streaming; 5) Security review completed for cross-tenant fragment reuse and KMS handling; 6) E2E tests and perf harness integrated into CI.
design_notes:
- Fingerprinting: use normalized UTF-8 canonicalization then a 64-bit content hash (xxHash64) with an additional context-salt to allow per-customer namespace when required.
- Normalization: strip non-deterministic tokens (timestamps, session ids), collapse repeated whitespace, and optionally apply a light semantic canonicalizer for long system prompts to increase dedupe recall.
- Fragment granularity: target 64-256 token shards; align fragments to 4MB GPU allocation buckets to make coalescing and contiguous GPU memory allocation easier.
- Index: compact in-memory hash map with bloom-filter pre-check to reduce remote index calls. Keep a small LRU of hot fragment entries per GPU.
- Attachment model: runtime attaches references to shared fragments into per-request KV descriptor; only the fragment descriptor is copied unless a write/patch is required (copy-on-write).
- Eviction: guided by access frequency, size, and predicted reuse window (learned from recent workload); consider periodic compaction that merges adjacent fragments when they have contiguous logical addresses and similar lifecycle.
- Multi-GPU: replicate very-hot fragments across GPUs on the node based on cost model; less-hot fragments use single-copy with fast RDMA/migration on attach.
- Safety: per-tenant isolation via context-salt and option to disable cross-tenant pooling. KMS usage for any fragments that include customer PII; fragments are scanned for PII patterns at ingestion when tenant settings require it.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (prototype): runtime-only change that computes normalized fingerprints at request ingest, consults local fragment index, and re-uses existing KV entries by reference. Implement copy-on-write when a request needs to patch a fragment. (Owner: Diego)
Phase 2 (kernel/gpu memory): align fragment allocations to GPU buckets and add coalescer that can compact adjacent fragments into contiguous GPU allocations during maintenance windows. (Owner: Nathan R.)
Phase 3 (replication + policies): implement hot-fragment replication across GPU partitions and the guided eviction daemon that consumes access telemetry. Add configuration knobs surfaced in Console. (Owner: Priya N.)
Phase 4 (hardening & rollout): security review, tenant opt-out flags, metrics, and gradual rollout behind feature flag with 10%->50%->100% progression. (Owner: PM: Arjun)

Approx PRs: runtime prototype (GH: redwood/runtime#BRANCH-fragment-pool-33210), gpu allocator changes (GH: redwood/kernel#BRANCH-gpu-coalescer-33210).
rollout_plan:
- Canary: enable on infra staging with synthetic workloads and real customer anonymized traces; monitor kv_fragment_hit_rate, kv_bytes_resident, p50/p95 latency, and token cost.
- Gradual ramp: 10% traffic (low-risk customers), evaluate 48h metrics, 50% traffic with broader workloads, then 100% if no regressions and security sign-off.
- Fall-back: on significant regression, runtime will refuse to attach pooled fragments and revert to per-request copies via feature flag.
- Communication: update Console release notes and internal runbook for on-call to disable feature and triage common causes.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: canonicalization, fingerprint collisions, copy-on-write semantics.
- Integration: runtime attaches shared fragments, perf harness simulating web-chat and instruction-following workloads.
- Chaos tests: GPU OOM injection during compaction, RDMA failure simulation during replication, verify graceful degradation.
- Perf benchmarks: run against 4x A100-80GB node cluster with concurrency sweep (qps 50->200) and measure kv hit amplification, memory-resident bytes, p50/p95 latency.
- Security tests: PII scanning opt-in checks and kdiff verification that fragments not allowed to leak across tenant boundaries.
metrics:
- kv_fragment_hit_rate: fraction of attaches satisfied by shared fragment reference; target >= 0.6 for chat workloads.
- kv_bytes_resident_per_gpu: target -20% compared to baseline.
- avg_fragment_attach_latency_ms: target <1ms additional overhead.
- token_cost_per_1M: expected reduction >=15% on dedupe-heavy workloads.
- p95_latency_streaming: regression <=5%.
risks:
- Fingerprint collisions: risk of incorrect reuse causing semantic leakage. Mitigation: 64-bit hash + length prefix + optional strong-check for high-value fragments.
- Privacy: reusing fragments across tenants could surface sensitive data. Mitigation: default per-tenant namespace and opt-in cross-tenant sharing after review.
- CPU overhead: normalization and hashing add CPU cost at request ingest. Mitigation: sample-based canonicalization and offload hashing to background thread pool.
- GPU fragmentation complexity: compaction introduces transient pause risk. Mitigation: do compaction incrementally and during low-traffic windows; use non-blocking GPU compaction primitives where available.
- Operational complexity: new knobs increase surface area; mitigate with Console defaults and telemetry dashboards.
comments: 2025-03-10 Maya Chen: Created ticket after spike showed repeated assistant-system prompts across 3 customers leading to ~30% duplicate KV storage. Added prototype plan and initial benchmarks.

2025-03-12 Lina Park: Design review - suggested adding bloom-filter pre-check to reduce index pressure and pushing normalization into a shared library to keep ingest path small. Also flagged tenant isolation requirement; requested security review ticket before rollout.

2025-03-13 Priya Nair: Implementation note - prioritize attach-by-reference to avoid per-token memcpy on hot path. We'll need changes in the descriptor format used by the kernel; will draft ABI proposal in GH.

2025-03-15 Tomás Green: Perf spike tests on staging 4xA100 show kv_bytes_resident down 24%, p95 down 6% at qps=120 for web-chat prompt set. CPU overhead for hashing ~0.8ms/request; acceptable for P1. Added follow-up to optimize normalization for micro-prompts.
2025-03-17 Arjun (PM): Security review queued. Blocking: confirm KMS workflow when fragment contents are tenant-encrypted. PJ from Security to audit fragment lifecycle (ingest->evict).
